questions.question: Which feature makes an organism living?
questions.explanation: The cell is the basic unit of life present in all living organisms.

questions.question: Organisms composed of a single cell are known as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Unicellular organisms consist of only one cell.

questions.question: Which of the following is the fundamental structural and functional unit of all living organisms?
questions.explanation: The cell is described as the fundamental structural and functional unit of life.

questions.question: Cells that lack a membrane bound nucleus are known as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic cells do not have a membrane bound nucleus.

questions.question: Which of the following is the semi-fluid matrix that occupies the volume of the cell?
questions.explanation: Cytoplasm is the semi-fluid matrix where cellular activities occur.

questions.question: Which structure contains the chromosomes and genetic material?
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains chromosomes which contain DNA.

questions.question: Which of the following is the main arena of cellular activities in both plant and animal cells?
questions.explanation: Various chemical reactions occur in the cytoplasm to keep the cell living.

questions.question: Which cells have a membrane bound nucleus?
questions.explanation: Eukaryotic cells have a membrane bound nucleus.

questions.question: Anything less than a complete cell structure fails to ensure which of the following?
questions.explanation: A complete cell structure is required for independent living.

questions.question: Which organism has the smallest cells?
questions.explanation: Mycoplasmas are the smallest cells at only 0.3 mm in length.

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest isolated single cell?
questions.explanation: The egg of an ostrich is the largest isolated single cell.

questions.question: Which of the following is the diameter of human red blood cells?
questions.explanation: Human red blood cells are about 7.0 µm in diameter.

questions.question: Which cells are some of the longest cells?
questions.explanation: Nerve cells are some of the longest cells.

questions.question: The shape of a cell may vary with which of the following?
questions.explanation: The shape of the cell may vary with the function they perform.

questions.question: Bacteria cells could be which of the following sizes?
questions.explanation: Bacteria could be 3 to 5 µm in size.

questions.question: Which organelle is the largest and most prominent in eukaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: The nucleus is the largest and most prominent organelle in eukaryotic cells.

questions.question: Which of the following is the double membrane structure that encloses the nucleus?
questions.explanation: The nuclear envelope is a double membrane that encloses the nucleus.

questions.question: Which of the following regulates molecular traffic between the nucleus and cytoplasm?
questions.explanation: Nuclear pores regulate molecular traffic between the nucleus and cytoplasm.

questions.question: The gel-like substance within the nucleus is called which of the following?
questions.explanation: Nucleoplasm is the gel-like substance containing chromatin and nucleoli.

questions.question: The nucleolus synthesizes which of the following?
questions.explanation: The nucleolus synthesizes ribosomal RNA.

questions.question: Which organelle is called the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondrion is often called the powerhouse of the cell.

questions.question: The folds of the inner mitochondrial membrane are called which of the following?
questions.explanation: The highly folded inner membrane forms cristae that project into the matrix.

questions.question: Mitochondria generate energy through which of the following processes?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria generate energy through oxidative phosphorylation and the electron transport chain.

questions.question: Which organelle has its own DNA allowing semi-autonomous replication?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria contain their own DNA allowing semi-autonomous replication.

questions.question: The endoplasmic reticulum exists in which two forms?
questions.explanation: The ER exists as rough ER and smooth ER.

questions.question: Which ER is studded with ribosomes?
questions.explanation: Rough ER is studded with ribosomes on its cytoplasmic surface.

questions.question: The function of smooth ER is which of the following?
questions.explanation: Smooth ER synthesizes lipids, phospholipids, and steroids.

questions.question: The flattened sacs of the Golgi apparatus are called which of the following?
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus consists of flattened membrane bound sacs called cisternae.

questions.question: Which face of the Golgi apparatus faces the ER?
questions.explanation: The cis face is the receiving side facing the ER.

questions.question: The Golgi apparatus is often called which of the following?
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus is often called the post office of the cell.

questions.question: Ribosomes are composed of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are composed of ribosomal RNA and proteins.

questions.question: Eukaryotic ribosomes are which type?
questions.explanation: Eukaryotic ribosomes are 80S type composed of 60S and 40S subunits.

questions.question: The primary function of ribosomes is which of the following?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes serve as the primary sites of protein synthesis.

questions.question: Lysosomes contain approximately how many hydrolytic enzymes?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes contain approximately 50 different hydrolytic enzymes.

questions.question: Lysosomal enzymes function optimally at which pH?
questions.explanation: Lysosomal enzymes function optimally at acidic pH around 5.

questions.question: The process of recycling cellular components by lysosomes is called which of the following?
questions.explanation: Autophagy is the recycling of cellular components by lysosomes.

questions.question: Peroxisomes contain which enzyme that breaks down hydrogen peroxide?
questions.explanation: Catalase breaks down hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen.

questions.question: Peroxisomes oxidize which of the following through beta-oxidation?
questions.explanation: Peroxisomes oxidize fatty acids through beta-oxidation.

questions.question: The cytoskeleton consists of how many main components?
questions.explanation: The cytoskeleton consists of microfilaments, intermediate filaments, and microtubules.

questions.question: The diameter of microfilaments is which of the following?
questions.explanation: Microfilaments are approximately 7 nm in diameter.

questions.question: Which cytoskeleton component forms hollow tubes?
questions.explanation: Microtubules are hollow tubes approximately 25 nm in diameter.

questions.question: According to the fluid mosaic model, the membrane is which of the following?
questions.explanation: The fluid mosaic model describes the membrane as dynamic with components that move laterally.

questions.question: In the phospholipid bilayer, which direction do hydrophobic tails face?
questions.explanation: Hydrophobic tails face inward while hydrophilic heads face outward.

questions.question: Which of the following maintains electrochemical gradients essential for nerve impulses?
questions.explanation: The cell membrane maintains electrochemical gradients essential for nerve impulses.

questions.question: Which of the following is the primary site of photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts are the primary site of photosynthesis.

questions.question: The stacks of thylakoids are called which of the following?
questions.explanation: Thylakoids are organized into structures called grana.

questions.question: Light-independent reactions occur in which part of chloroplasts?
questions.explanation: Light-independent reactions occur in the stroma.

questions.question: The plant cell wall is primarily composed of which of the following?
questions.explanation: The plant cell wall is composed primarily of cellulose fibers.

questions.question: Which membrane surrounds the central vacuole?
questions.explanation: The central vacuole is surrounded by a membrane called the tonoplast.

questions.question: The central vacuole can occupy which percentage of cell volume?
questions.explanation: The central vacuole can occupy 30 to 90 percent of the total cell volume.
